characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku D/Max-2200 X-ray Diffractometer, Cu target operated at 40 kV and 40 mA with a graphite monochromator, radiation wavelength λ = 0.154056 nm
characterization_methods.key_findings: The as-cast 0Cr strip mainly consists of austenite and ferrite; a double peak between 43.5° and 45.0° corresponds to (110)δ and (220)DO3.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scanning angle 30°–100°, continuous scanning with a speed of 4°/min
characterization_methods.purpose: phase identification of the as-cast (and annealed) low-density steel strips

characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregularly shaped δ-ferrite (short rod-shape in the as-cast 0Cr strip) is distributed in the γ-austenite matrix; the volume fraction of δ-ferrite in the as-cast 0Cr steel strip is 3%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: after mechanical polishing and etching (3.3 vol% nitric acid + 3.3 vol% acetic acid + 0.1 vol% hydrofluoric acid, etching time 3 s); SEM photographs taken at a position 0.5 mm from the strip surface along the thickness direction
characterization_methods.purpose: characterize the microstructure, morphology and volume fraction of δ-ferrite

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL-2010F operated at 200 kV; specimens prepared by twin-jet electrolytic polishing at −30 °C and 30 V with a mixed solution of 10% perchloric acid and 90% alcohol
characterization_methods.key_findings: In the as-cast 0Cr strip, κ-carbides with volume fraction 3% and average size 6 nm are present in the γ-austenite; the δ-ferrite contains DO3 ordered phase of size 26 ± 3 nm; measured lattice parameters are 0.387 nm (κ-carbide) and 0.375 nm (γ-austenite).
characterization_methods.purpose: elucidate the nano-scale precipitated phases (κ-carbides in γ-austenite and DO3 in δ-ferrite)
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) with selected-area diffraction patterns (SADP)

measure the average phase fraction of the steel strips

interfaces.phase_evolution: In the as-cast condition a double peak between 43.5° and 45.0° ((110)δ and (220)DO3) is present; the Cr element promotes the transformation from δ-ferrite to the ordered DO3 phase (relevant context for the 0Cr strip).

phase_interfaces.coherence: orientation relationship of [110] // [110] between κ-carbide and γ-austenite

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 100 g alloy ingot was prepared by melting 99.99% pure iron, 99.9% pure manganese, 99.9% pure aluminum, 99.9% pure chromium and 99.8% high-purity graphite by a cold-crucible levitation melting setup (x=0 for the 0Cr steel).

The ingot was remelted by induction melting and the molten metal was poured into a copper mold rotating at 600 rpm, yielding as-cast steel strips of 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm. The near-rapid solidification was carried out under an argon atmosphere at a cooling rate of 1–1 × 10^4 K/s.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests performed at least 3 times by a MTS Criterion 44 Mechanical Property Tester; specimens machined from the steel strips.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm

strain_hardening_rate.value: the as-cast 0Cr (Cr-free) strain hardening rate curve exhibits a 'hump', similar to the hump associated with deformation twinning in a TWIP steel

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Measured by an AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer.

phases_present.morphology: short rod-shape / irregularly shaped, distributed in the γ-austenite matrix

phases_present.crystal_structure: ordered body-centered cubic (space group Fm3m), lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm in the ferrite
phases_present.morphology: ordered nano-scale precipitates in the δ-ferrite

structures.overall_structure: γ-austenite matrix with irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributed in it; the ferrite is short rod-shaped in the as-cast 0Cr strip. Nano-scale κ-carbides precipitate in the γ-austenite and an ordered DO3 phase forms in the δ-ferrite.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the as-cast 0Cr steel strip (wt.%): Mn 20.43, Al 9.16, C 1.17, Cr 0, S 0.0006, Fe Bal. (Table 1).
The product of ultimate tensile strength and total elongation (UTS × TE) for the as-cast 0Cr steel strip is 34.0 GPa % (Table 2).
Measured lattice parameters in the as-cast 0Cr steel strip: κ-carbide = 0.387 nm and γ-austenite = 0.375 nm.

The ideal stoichiometry of the κ-carbide is (Fe, Mn)3AlC with a perovskite crystal structure; Fe or Mn atoms occupy the cornered positions, Al atoms occupy the face-center positions, and C is in the center of the cube (½, ½, ½).

The ordered DO3 phase in the ferrite is a body-centered cubic crystal with a lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm, in which Fe or Mn atoms occupy cornered positions and Al or Fe/Mn atoms occupy every other centered positions.

The annealing treatment increases the yield strength of 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr steel strips by 131 MPa, 277 MPa and 141 MPa respectively (cited increment for 0Cr = 131 MPa; concerns the annealed state, not the as-cast sample).
